Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between high and low grade IPMN and between high grade IPMN and ND. From the commonly upregulated proteins, nominate a few important genes that are related to Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the literature.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A total of 7,624 proteins were quantified by glycoproteomics and proteomics in 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs, 5 IOPNs) versus 76 normal ducts (ND). We filtered for proteins significantly up in both high-grade (HG) versus low-grade (LG) IPMN (FDR < 0.05, log2FC > 0) and HG IPMN versus ND (FDR < 0.05, log2FC > 0), yielding 279 commonly upregulated proteins.

Keywords  
– Autophagy / ATG9A  
– Cell cycle / MCM7  
– Amino acid transport / SLC1A5  
– Metastasis/glycoprotein / CDCP1  
– Secreted factors / TFF3  

Candidate Genes  
From the 279, we nominate:  
• TFF3 (HG vs LG 3.10; HG vs ND 4.77)  
• SLC1A5 (1.40; 1.73)  
• ATG9A (1.08; 2.02)  
• CDCP1 (1.02; 1.11)  
• MCM7 (0.91; 0.89)

Literature Validation & Nomination  
• MCM7: a minichromosome-maintenance complex member; upregulated in HG IPMN (log2FC 0.91) and early PDAC prognostic marker post-pancreaticoduodenectomy (PMCID: PMC6130532).  
• TFF3: strongest fold-change (HG vs ND 4.77) but no direct PDAC publications in Rummagene query.  
• SLC1A5: key glutamine transporter supporting tumor metabolism; no PDAC articles retrieved by our tool but established in other solid tumors.  
• ATG9A: autophagy regulator with high network centrality (composite 0.76); emerging in cancer–metabolism links but no direct PDAC hits.  
• CDCP1: cell-surface glycoprotein implicated in metastasis; limited PDAC–specific literature via our query but known in pancreatic cancer biology.
